_comment: Secretary config. Everything you'd want to tune lives here — no code changes needed. Restart the server, or POST /api/config/reload, after editing.

ai._comment: The model is used for exactly two things: classifying emails that already passed your rules, and writing one summary line. Set provider to 'off' to run the whole system with zero AI calls — the brief still works.

schedule._comment: Every source is pulled on one clock. The model is not on this clock: priorities are cached against a hash of the open work, so a 15-minute cycle costs nothing extra when nothing changed.

brief._maxRepeats_note: After this many briefs an unchanged, undated item goes QUIET: it still appears in its lane, collapsed behind a "show N quieter" toggle. Anything with a deadline, or written in CAPS, is never quieted.
brief._horizonDays_note: Anything dated further out than this waits its turn. Nothing else is ever removed — repeated items are marked quiet and collapsed, not dropped.

brightspace._comment: Secondary enrichment layer: syllabus grading/topic context on items you tap, plus a count of Brightspace deadlines with no matching Google Calendar entry yet. Never a replacement for Calendar — see backend/sources/brightspace.js.
brightspace._enabled_note: The .ics URL itself lives in .env as BRIGHTSPACE_ICS_URL (run `npm run set-brightspace-url`), never here — it's a credential, and .env is the one file that never travels between machines on a git pull. This flag alone doesn't gate anything in code yet; it's here for when a manual pause switch is worth adding.
brightspace._syllabiDir_note: Where `npm run parse-syllabi` looks for PDFs. Already covered by backend/data/'s own .gitignore rule — syllabus PDFs never get committed.
brightspace._auditWindowDays_note: How far out the "not on your calendar yet" count looks. A Brightspace deadline further out than this isn't counted as missing — it's just not due soon enough to flag yet.
brightspace._courseCodeMatchWindowDays_note: A Brightspace item counts as already-scheduled if a calendar item with the same course code falls within this many days of it — loose enough that your own reminder a day early (or the Brightspace cutoff being a day later than your own entry) still counts as a match.

categories._comment: How the system decides what KIND of thing something is. Every match is collected and the heaviest weight wins, so an exam on the 'School & Classes' calendar is still a Test. Nothing in the code knows your calendar names — this is the only place they appear.
categories._matching: calendarPatterns match the calendar's name, titlePatterns match the event title or email subject, tiers match an email's rule tier. All are case-insensitive substring matches.

domains._comment: Which lane of your life something belongs to. This is what the brief is GROUPED by, and it is deliberately separate from category: 'CANNOT MISS' tells you how much something matters, not whether it's an exam or a friend's wedding.
domains._matching: calendarPatterns are checked first across all domains, then titlePatterns, then pathPatterns (for vault notes). If nothing matches, fromCategory supplies a hint, then fallback.
domains._fromCategory_note: Categories that are about IMPORTANCE rather than subject (critical, important, deadline) are deliberately absent — they should never decide a lane, so those items fall through to pattern matching.

ranking._comment: Added on top of the category weight to produce one score per item. Every contribution is recorded on the item as _rankWhy, so you can always see why something ranked where it did.
ranking._emphasisBoost_note: You write things in CAPS when they matter. A title that is ≥70% uppercase (and longer than 3 letters) gets this, so your own convention is respected without listing any specific event.

email._minScore_note: Emails scoring below this never reach the model. Lower it to widen the net, raise it to spend less.
email._boost_note: Terms marked searchBody below are sent to Gmail as a full-text query, so mail that mentions your workplace deep in the body, or is signed by a colleague at the bottom, is caught without downloading a single message. Costs one extra id-list call per tier.

rules._comment: Priority order you set: opportunities first, then work and family, then school.
rules._people_note: searchBody also finds them in signatures. Only distinctive terms (7+ characters, or a multi-word phrase) are ever body-searched — 'mom' and 'dad' would match half the inbox, so they stay header-only.

calendar._note: The calendar's own name is never printed in the brief — for the default calendar that name is your email address, which tells you nothing. It's used to derive the category chip instead.

dismissal._comment: No single dismiss — your own click, or the system's own automatic 'this looks gone' guess — makes an item vanish forever on the first try. Every dismiss counts a strike; only after this many strikes on the SAME item does it lock in for good (permanentlySuppressed). Below that, a dismissed item can still come back on its own if it turns out to be a wrong guess, or if its content genuinely changes. Use scripts/force-dismiss.js, or the 'suppress' action, to skip the count and lock something in immediately instead of waiting it out.

money._comment: Money speaks only when one of these fires. Most days it says nothing.
money._contributionDayOfMonth_note: Set to a day (e.g. 1) to get a reminder. Leave null to disable.
money._baseCurrency_note: Everything is converted to this at the live rate before any total or weight is computed. USD and CAD positions used to be summed raw, which made every number on the money page wrong.
money._holdings_note: Shares come from the vault's `type: holding` notes, so the book follows what you actually maintain. config/portfolio.json is only a fallback.
money._holdingsRefreshDays_note: The vault is only re-read the first time a pull is checked after local midnight (config.timezone), not on a rolling N-hours-since-last-time clock — a sync at 11:58 PM won't push the next one to nearly midnight the following day. Raise this to check less often than daily. Run `npm run sync-holdings` for an immediate forced refresh after editing a holding note.
money._stockIdeaCount_note: How many candidates show on the money page's 'worth a look' spot. Ranked by lib/stockIdeas.js — real Yahoo similarity data plus your real sector weights, never an AI pitch.
money._stockIdeaShortlist_note: How many candidates get the (more expensive) sector+price lookup before ranking. Raise it to consider more candidates per refresh; lower it to spend fewer Yahoo calls.
money._stockIdeaRefreshDays_note: Same calendar-day cadence as holdingsRefreshDays, same lib/time.js math: a new candidate shows up the first time this is checked after local midnight, not on a rolling 24-hours-since-last-time clock. Raise this for less-than-daily (e.g. 3 = every third day). `npm run refresh-stock-idea` forces an immediate refresh regardless of this setting.
money._stockIdeaConcentrationPenalty_note: 0 = ignore sector weight entirely, rank purely on Yahoo similarity. 1 = a candidate in a sector you're already heavily weighted in is discounted almost to zero. This is the main tuning knob for 'smart, not random' vs. 'actually helps rebalance.'
money._stockIdeaSummarySentences_note: How many sentences of Yahoo's own business-summary blurb show under a candidate — the plain-English 'what does this company actually do' line. Straight from Yahoo's text, nothing rewritten or generated.
money._stockIdeaSummaryMaxChars_note: Hard length cap on that summary regardless of sentence count, so one run-on sentence can't blow out the layout.
money._stockIdeaScreenerId_note: The 'discover beyond your portfolio' half of the pick, alongside the similarity-based half above. One of Yahoo's predefined screens: aggressive_small_caps, small_cap_gainers, undervalued_growth_stocks, growth_technology_stocks, most_actives, day_gainers, day_losers, undervalued_large_caps. Small-cap ones lean toward genuinely unfamiliar names; the gainer/mover ones lean toward 'something's happening today.'
money._stockIdeaScreenerShortlist_note: How many candidates to pull from the screener and carry into enrichment/ranking, same idea as stockIdeaShortlist above but for the screener source.
money._stockIdeaMaxMarketCap_note: Hard ceiling in raw market cap (not FX-adjusted — a USD and a CAD cap are compared against the same number, so treat this as approximate). Anything above it is excluded outright, from either source. This exists specifically so a mega-cap you basically already know about (a big bank, a big telecom) can't be the pick — that's what was happening before this existed.
money._stockIdeaAnalystUpsideWeight_note: How much Yahoo's analyst price targets (financialData.targetMeanPrice vs. the live price) move the ranking, clamped to ±30%/60% so one stale outlier target can't dominate. 0 = ignore analyst targets entirely. A candidate with no analyst coverage at all (common for small-caps) gets no adjustment either way — missing data isn't a penalty.
money._stockIdeaNoRepeatDays_note: How many past picks stay excluded from re-selection. Keeps a static portfolio from just re-deriving the same answer every morning. 0 disables the no-repeat check entirely.

display._comment: The three-page screen at /display. Small, mostly looked-at rather than operated — but there IS a cursor and a refresh button, because the same URL is how you debug the pipeline on a laptop.
display._days_note: How many days after today to show. 3 fits a 1024x600 panel; an 800x480 panel drops the third automatically.
display._movers_note: Top N risers and fallers in the portfolio snapshot.
display._staleAfterHours_note: Pulls run every 15 min, so anything older than an hour means something is broken, not merely quiet.
display._pages_note: Three pages: Today (timeline), Tasks, Money. Arrow keys or the dots move between them; the deck also rotates on its own.
display._rotateSeconds_note: Auto-advance interval for the always-on screen. Any mouse move or key press pauses rotation for a while, so it never yanks the page out from under you on a laptop. Set 0 to disable.
display._undatedMaxAgeDays_note: How many days an undated Start-here candidate stays eligible before it ages out on its own, provided it has not been marked done or dismissed. Dated items are unaffected — their own due date decides that.

vault._watchFolders_note: Case-insensitive path prefixes. Archive, Journal and anything with `sensitive: true` are never read, per the vault's own AGENTS.md rules.
